Subject: SprintBridge: Orchestration playbook & staged adoption (MAP)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for signing. Attached is our proposed orchestration playbook embedded into the MAP for SprintBridge (attached: SprintBridge_MAP_v1.0.xlsx) and an operational deployment runbook (deployment_runbook_v1.pdf). This is a lightweight, staged plan designed to get the first production canary live with minimal risk and then scale to full migration across your region. Key points at a glance:

- Kickoff: week of 2028-05-22 (proposed) — 1.5hr technical kickoff + stakeholder alignment
- Canary cohort A: 5% traffic, 48hr monitoring window, rollback triggers defined in canary-checklist.md
- Migration wave 1: 25% traffic, scheduled off-peak window (US Pacific) — 2028-06-05 02:00–06:00 PT
- Training: two live sessions (admin + ops) followed by on-demand recordings
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to hosted model variant, manual rollback option via runbook

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) Confirm kickoff date and attendees (technical + product + ops)
2) Confirm Canary window & preferred migration weekend
3) Marissa will send detailed sprint-level MAP with responsible owners and acceptance criteria

Attachments: SprintBridge_MAP_v1.0.xlsx, deployment_runbook_v1.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Jonas Weber
Principal Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Alex — thanks for the quick turn. A few operational details I’ve locked down and are reflected in the attached canary-checklist.md (cc: attachment):

- Canary cohort A details: 5% production traffic routed to Redwood dedicated pool; health checks: latency p50/p95, error rate threshold 0.5% over 10-minute window, quality regression check against reference eval set (prompt set SB_REF_1).
- Observability: we’ll add per-route tracing and a temporary slack channel (#sprintbridge-canary) for 72 hours post-cutover for live alerts.
- Rollback criteria: (1) sustained p95 latency > 1.8x baseline for 30m, (2) token error rate > 0.5% over 10m, (3) manual sign-off from SprintBridge SRE.
- Migration waves: wave 1 -> 25% on 2028-06-05 02:00–05:00 PT; wave 2 -> 50% (one week later); full -> after acceptance gate.

Action items for SprintBridge:
- Confirm SRE and product owners for acceptance gate by Friday 2028-05-19
- Approve canary thresholds or propose alternatives

I’ll push an updated MAP workbook (v1.1) after we confirm attendees.

Marissa Cole
Senior Implementation Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Alex / team —

Couple of technical/contract items to call out before kickoff:

1) Dedicated capacity request: to guarantee canary throughput we recommend pre-warming a small dedicated pool starting 2028-05-30. This avoids cold-start behavior during the canary. Please confirm if SprintBridge will take a short, prepaid reserved slot for the first two weeks of June.

2) SLA exceptions & fallback model: we’ll configure automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted model variant in case of regional capacity issues. This preserves availability but may have slightly different latency/quality — we’ll surface any quality diffs in the MAP acceptance tests.

3) Security/Networking: Priya — please confirm whether you’ll provide a VPC peering window or we should plan on API-based secure routing. If VPC peering, we’ll need a maintenance window to exchange routing ACLs (target: 2028-05-29 10:00–12:00 PT).

4) Procurement/documents: we see DocuSign is in-flight (link below). Once countersigned, please share the HubSpot deal id to attach to the MAP.

Relevant links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567 (HubSpot), https://www.docusign.com/recipient/ABCDEF1234567890

I’ll be available on the kickoff call to walk through rollback play and dedicated-pool scaling.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Dedicated Deployments | Redwood Inference
